newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Euro bourses stay ahead, dollar mixed.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euro bourses stay ahead, dollar mixed.

text.p: European bourses, nervous over the outlook for Wall Street, the world's leading stock market, advanced in morning trading on Wednesday after a rebound in New York and welcome news on U.S. interest rates.
On the foreign exchanges, the dollar slipped against the yen but rose versus the mark as Japanese trade figures and German money supply data moved it in different directions.
London share traders said trading was likely to be thin ahead of the Christmas holidays.

"We've had a good, if predictable morning," the head of sales and trading at a large brokerage said. "But volumes are nothing to speak about. We've seen some selective buying but otherwise it's been pretty quiet."
Investors continue to fret about the risk of a more pronounced drop on Wall Street, which still shows a 26 percent advance this year, even after recent weakness, dealers said.
Adding to question marks over U.S. share prospects, top stategists at Merrill Lynch said investors might be better off with bonds instead of stocks next year.

But the London stock market, Europe's busiest, was not looking too far ahead for now. It gained 0.9 percent in the morning, shrugging off a larger-than-expected drop in British jobless numbers, which prompted fears of higher interest rates.

The market took its cue, instead, from Wall Street's latest performance and continued bid speculation. News of an agreed 1.267 billion pound ($2.11 billion) bid by U.S. group Entergy for London Electricity set the market rumour mills running.

But the news that British November unemployment fell 95,800 to 1.93 million -- much more than a forecast 26,000 decline -- and that retail sales rose 0.7 percent rather than a forecast 0.5 percent jolted the bond market.
"(It is) very strong data which will certainly increase pressure on the Chancellor(of Exchequer Kenneth Clarke)to increase rates," said Andrew Snowball, economist at the Cooperative Bank.

Wall Street on Tuesday recovered from early losses after the Federal Reserve, as generally expected, kept interest rates unchanged. The Dow Jones industrial average closed up 39.98 points at 6,308.33, erasing Monday's losses.
But U.S. bond prices fell on surprisingly strong November U.S. housing starts, which prompted some nervousness on interest rates further ahead.

In Paris shares were aided by the Dow's gains and buoyed by prospects for lower French interest rates. Wall Street's revival helped German shares make a firm start, too, as did a firmer dollar -- good news for exporters -- and weaker-than-expected German money supply data.
The Bundesbank said growth in its main monetary policy indicator, M3 money supply, slowed to an annualised rate of 8.0 percent in November from 8.4 percent in October.
Economists said it did not change their view that the central bank was unlikely to amend its policy just now.
The currency market, however, lived in hope of lower German rates and boosted the dollar against the mark as a result.
"The M3 data was just soft enough to keep interest in Thursday's meeting alive," said one trader at a British bank.
The Bundesbank central council meets for the last time this year on Thursday and is set to announce its 1997 M3 growth targets at a news conference afterwards.

Analysts said there was a slight chance the bank might shave its 3.0 percent securities repurchase rate. Market speculation on such a move grew after the Bank of France trimmed its key money rate to 3.15 percent from 3.20 on Tuesday.
On Wednesday, French call money eased to 3-3/16 5/16 from 3-1/4 3/8, giving hope of more rate reductions, analysts said.
The pound, meanwhile, rallied after the strong British data to $1.6733 and 2.5981 marks from 1.6713 and 2.5845 overnight.
Currency trading was, however, thin ahead of the holidays. "The Japanese trade data is the main story but the market is struggling to find an interest," said Adrian Schmidt at Chase.
The yen strengthened after news of an unexpected 0.2 percent year-on-year rise in Japan's custom-cleared trade surplus and a sharp 31.2 percent rise in its surplus with the United States.
CURRENCIES AT 1200 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.5528 marks and 113.60 yen, compared with 1.5454 and 113.73 in late business on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1200 GMT
London's FTSE 100 index was up 34.6 at 4,014.2.
In Frankfurt, the 30-share DAX was 9.14 higher at 2,824.27. In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was up 25.41 at 2,219.11.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $369 and then rose to $369.30 versus the previous close of $368.95. Silver was one cent lower at $4.86.
